correctness.rationale: Both factors have constant term 1 and only residues 0/1 mod h. For h>=3 simultaneous residue-1 terms are impossible, forcing a pure-residue factor. The common cofactor can be replaced by a full window; the bounded-gap composition bijection gives c_b, and independent residue rows yield its square. Disjoint cases exhaust all divisors, including n=1 and a=0. The h=2,n=2 boundary was enumerated. Verification code cross-checks finite instances, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Binary lunar divisor counts on regular but nonconstant digit patterns are a natural and difficult arithmetic enumeration problem highlighted by Applegate et al. The result gives a complete exact count for every repeated two-on/long-gap pattern, explains surprising gap independence, yields a quadratic second-moment refinement of the classical repunit composition formula, and sharply identifies the first admissible gap. This is more than a variable substitution because factors can occupy two residue rows subject to a shared cofactor.
